sources.author: le
sources.title: A Meta-Protocol for Cooperation · Adaptive Persistence summary for Analogue Group
sources.description: A ten-page summary by Stephen Le, last updated 11 October 2026: the challenge of cooperation, the Persistence Framework, the five-step meta-protocol, 24 design principles across coordination, adaptability and robustness, the ACT group matrix, formats for adjustment and four case studies from his facilitation. The case studies are the author’s own reports. Page numbers refer to the PDF.

sources.author: le
sources.title: Adaptive Persistence overview
sources.description: A three-page overview by Stephen Le, last updated 30 September 2026: the framework’s three questions, who can use it and its six-step process. An earlier companion to the summary. Page numbers refer to the PDF.

goal.title: Cooperate, adapt, withstand, and fit the world
goal.summary: Adaptive Persistence’s three questions become three conditions, with a fourth: the group’s capacities have to match its environment. The supporting conditions are drawn from the summary’s 24 design principles.

current_reality.title: Why conflict keeps coming back
current_reality.summary: Pressure for visible progress and fear of vulnerability together keep fixes on the surface, while free riders wear down cooperation. Candidate causes to test in a real group.

conflict.title: Open up, or keep your guard?
conflict.summary: Real cooperation needs people to say what gets in the way; a competitive field punishes anyone who shows weakness. The summary proposes ways to soften the choice rather than settle it.

future_reality.title: Find the mismatch, then close it
future_reality.summary: The cycle and the summary’s rule of thumb together show which capacity the environment calls for. Combined with what members finally say, adjustments can reach causes.

future_reality.title: Say what gets in the way
future_reality.summary: The ACT matrix, or a lighter first pass for wary groups, can bring hidden needs into the open and win members’ part in the fix. The author reports four cases; they are not independent evidence.

future_reality.title: Agree what success means
future_reality.summary: The summary asks each group to set clear success criteria when it orients and to stop once they are met. No connection to the other changes is recorded yet.

prerequisite.title: Agree the issue, then gather the data
prerequisite.summary: A group first needs one issue nobody objects to, with success criteria, and then a shared description of its environment and capacities.

prerequisite.title: Make it safe to adjust
prerequisite.summary: Leading the matrix takes training, and wary groups need their own vocabulary. The format then has to suit the group's size and trust.

transition.title: Orient
transition.summary: Agree one issue and what success would look like.

transition.title: Assess
transition.summary: Gather information on the environment and the group's capacities.

transition.title: Analyse
transition.summary: Choose the capacity the environment most calls for.

transition.title: Adjust
transition.summary: Work through the matrix in a format that suits the group.

transition.title: Repeat
transition.summary: Reassess, and stop once the success criteria are met.

overview.title: Cooperate, adapt, withstand, and fit the world
overview.text: Adaptive Persistence asks three questions of a group: can we cooperate, can we adapt, can we tolerate disruption? A fourth condition is that the mix suits how volatile, hazardous and varied the group’s environment is.
link: Inspect the goal and its supporting conditions →

overview.title: Fixes that treat symptoms
overview.text: Pressure for visible progress and fear of vulnerability keep fixes on the surface, so conflict returns. Free riders make cooperation hard to sustain.

overview.title: A dilemma a group has to work through
overview.text: Openness and self-protection pull against each other in a competitive field. This is a proposed reading of the sources, offered for a real group to test.

overview.title: Find the mismatch, then close it
overview.text: Assess the environment and the group’s capacities, emphasise the capacity the environment calls for, and use the ACT matrix to bring what really gets in the way into the open, with success criteria agreed at the start.

overview.title: An agreed issue and a safe way to adjust
overview.text: A group needs one issue nobody objects to, shared data on its environment and capacities, someone trained to lead the matrix, and a format and vocabulary that suit it. These are proposed readiness conditions, not completed preparations.
link: Review the obstacles and intermediate objectives →

overview.title: Orient, assess, analyse, adjust, repeat
overview.text: The summary’s five steps, as an illustrative sequence for one group. The existing conditions are examples, not observations; no group, facilitator, owner or date is assigned.

overview.title: From the Persistence Framework to what a group can do
overview.text: Stephen Le’s Persistence Framework joins Adaptive Persistence, a protocol for cooperation, with Procedural Ethics and Persistent Systems Theory. This map follows the protocol as the two Adaptive Persistence documents describe it.

overview.title: Stephen Le’s Adaptive Persistence
overview.text: Persistent Systems Theory and Adaptive Persistence are Stephen Le’s, and both credited documents are his. The AI is responsible for selecting, paraphrasing and connecting the material. Every item has a page locator and a labelled basis; source credit is not author endorsement.

nodes.text: A group persists through time and does well in the environment it actually faces: it meets its aims, keeps its members' trust and well-being, and resolves its conflicts.
nodes.label: A group lasts and does well in its environment.

nodes.text: Members can cooperate: the group manages the dynamics among its members well.
nodes.label: Members manage the dynamics among them.

nodes.text: The group adapts well to changes in its external environment.
nodes.label: It adapts to changes in its environment.

nodes.text: The group withstands severe shocks.
nodes.label: It withstands severe shocks.

nodes.text: Its mix of coordination, adaptation and robustness matches the environment it faces.
nodes.label: Its capacities match its environment.

source_refs.locator: p. 3, steps 3 and 4: Analyze and Adjust

nodes.text: Decisions are efficient and inclusive, and conflicts are resolved efficiently and effectively.
nodes.label: Decisions are inclusive and conflicts get resolved.

source_refs.locator: p. 5, collaboration principles c and d

nodes.text: Benefits and costs are fairly shared, and breaches of agreed norms are visible and met with proportionate sanctions.
nodes.label: Costs and benefits are fair; norms are visibly upheld.

source_refs.locator: pp. 4–5, collaboration principles b, e and g

nodes.text: The group watches its environment continuously and combines scattered information into a picture that supports decisions.
nodes.label: It watches its environment and makes sense of it.

source_refs.locator: p. 5, adaptability principles a and e

nodes.text: The group tests new ideas at limited scale, avoids depending on one solution too early and learns quickly from the consequences.
nodes.label: It tries small bets and learns from them quickly.

source_refs.locator: p. 5, adaptability principles b, g and h

nodes.text: The group keeps spare financial, material, human and operational capacity, and can restore essential operations after a disruption.
nodes.label: It keeps spare capacity and can recover.

source_refs.locator: p. 5, robustness principles b and c

nodes.text: Local failures do not cascade through the whole group, and it is settled in advance who decides during a disruption.
nodes.label: Failures stay local; crisis authority is clear.

source_refs.locator: p. 5, robustness principles e, f and g

nodes.text: The group knows how volatile, hazardous and varied its environment is.
nodes.label: It knows how volatile, hazardous and varied its world is.

source_refs.locator: p. 2, 2. Assess environment: volatility, hazardousness, heterogeneity
p. 2, decrease the mismatch between environment and core characteristics

backlog.label: Ask Stephen Le whether this goal states what Adaptive Persistence is for.
backlog.note: The goal joins his stated aims (performance, well-being and trust, fewer conflicts) with lasting through time. He has not reviewed the wording.

nodes.text: Leaders under pressure to show immediate, visible progress reach for quick fixes rather than probing the structural factors that undermine cooperation.
nodes.label: Pressure for visible progress favours quick fixes.

source_refs.locator: p. 2, The Challenge of Cooperation: myopia

nodes.text: Competitive fields such as business, sport, security and the military actively discourage people from being vulnerable and revealing their needs.
nodes.label: Competitive settings discourage vulnerability.

source_refs.locator: p. 3, The Persistence Framework; p. 7, ACT and EFT

nodes.text: Members feel too unsafe to be vulnerable and reveal their real needs, so assessments rarely reach what people actually think and feel.
nodes.label: Fear keeps real needs hidden.

source_refs.locator: p. 2, fear; p. 7, why bother with ACT

nodes.text: The group has not assessed how volatile and hazardous its environment is, so it cannot tell which capacity it is short of.
nodes.label: It hasn't assessed its environment.

source_refs.locator: p. 3, existing frameworks address specific aspects; p. 6, 3. Analyze

nodes.text: Fixes address superficial concerns while the mismatch between the group's capacities and its environment remains.
nodes.label: Fixes treat symptoms; the mismatch remains.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, the problem with quick solutions

nodes.text: Free riders take advantage of other people’s cooperation, making it hard to sustain in the long run.
nodes.label: Free riders make cooperation hard to sustain.

nodes.text: Friction and conflict keep returning between members or units, and trust and morale fall.
nodes.label: Conflict keeps returning; trust and morale fall.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, fall into conflict and low morale again
p. 2, myopia and fear; p. 7, quick solutions and fear
p. 7, the group will soon fall into conflict and low morale again

backlog.label: Check in one real group whether quick fixes leave the mismatch in place.
backlog.note: The summary states this from its author's facilitation experience; alternative explanations for recurring conflict have not been examined.

nodes.text: The group cooperates well enough to persist in a competitive field.
nodes.label: It cooperates well enough to compete.

nodes.text: Members need to trust one another enough to say what really gets in the way.
nodes.label: Members need to say what really gets in the way.

nodes.text: Members need to protect their standing in a field that punishes weakness.
nodes.label: Members need to protect their standing.

nodes.text: Members are open and vulnerable about their real thoughts, feelings and needs.
nodes.label: Be open and vulnerable.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, ACT and EFT help people become more open and vulnerable

nodes.text: Members keep their guard up and avoid showing vulnerability.
nodes.label: Keep your guard up.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, our basic instinct in fearful situations is to maintain our guard
p. 7, access their inner thoughts and feelings

assumptions.text: Any expression of need will be read as weakness, whatever words it is put in.

source_refs.locator: pp. 3 and 7, competitive environments discourage vulnerability

nodes.text: The group runs the Adaptive Persistence cycle: orient on one agreed issue, assess its environment and core capacities, analyse the mismatch, adjust, and repeat.
nodes.label: Assess, close the biggest mismatch, and repeat.

nodes.text: Emphasise adaptability where the environment is volatile, robustness where it is hazardous, and coordination where it is neither.
nodes.label: Emphasise the capacity the environment calls for.

nodes.text: Work through the ACT group matrix: the values behind the chosen capacity, how the group would act if it improved, the thoughts and feelings that get in the way, and how to move forward while acknowledging them.
nodes.label: Name what gets in the way, and move anyway.

nodes.text: For groups wary of vulnerability, word the matrix in their own vocabulary and begin with a lighter first pass before a deeper one.
nodes.label: Start lighter where vulnerability feels unsafe.

nodes.text: Agree clear success criteria at the start, test each cycle against them, and stop once they are met.
nodes.label: Agree success criteria and test against them.

nodes.text: The group sees which capacity its environment most calls for and where it falls short.
nodes.label: It sees which capacity it is short of.

nodes.text: Members voice the thoughts, feelings and needs that a structural assessment misses.
nodes.label: Hidden needs get voiced.

nodes.text: Members become willing to take an active part in finding the solution.
nodes.label: Members take part in the fix.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, obtain their willingness and active participation

nodes.text: Adjustments address structural causes rather than symptoms.
nodes.label: Fixes reach causes, not symptoms.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, the problem with quick solutions

nodes.text: Members cooperate, and conflicts are resolved rather than recurring.
nodes.label: Conflict gets resolved, not repeated.

source_refs.locator: p. 2, greater trust, well-being and performance

nodes.text: The group's capacities fit its environment better with each cycle.
nodes.label: Capacities fit the environment better each cycle.

nodes.text: Stephen Le reports four facilitation cases, using lighter variations of the method, in which groups in conflict reconciled or renewed their collaboration.
nodes.label: Le reports four cases where groups reconciled.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, access their inner thoughts and feelings and obtain their willingness
p. 7, Assess gathers structural problems; ACT reaches inner needs
p. 3, changes implemented in-house are more sustainable

nodes.text: The group can run one full Adaptive Persistence cycle on an issue it cares about.
nodes.label: The group can run one full cycle.

nodes.text: Members disagree about which issue matters most.
nodes.label: Members disagree on the main issue.

source_refs.locator: p. 4, Sometimes there will be disagreement on the main issue

nodes.text: The group agrees one main issue that nobody objects to, can be evaluated, is stated positively, is achievable through action and applies to everyone, with clear success criteria.
nodes.label: One agreed main issue with success criteria.

nodes.text: There is no information yet about the environment or the group's core capacities.
nodes.label: There is no data on environment or capacities.

nodes.text: Interviews, surveys and existing records describe the environment's volatility and hazard and the group's coordination, adaptability and robustness principles.
nodes.label: Assessments describe the environment and capacities.

nodes.text: Members feel too unsafe to say what they really think.
nodes.label: Members feel too unsafe to speak.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, too unsafe to risk being vulnerable

nodes.text: An adjustment format suits the group's size and trust: talking for small high-trust groups, email for small low-trust ones, the matrix with meetings, or voting for large groups.
nodes.label: A format that fits the group's size and trust.

source_refs.locator: p. 8, Formats for carrying out adjustment

nodes.text: ACT and similar methods take training and a lot of practice to lead.
nodes.label: Leading the method takes training.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, ACT and EFT are fairly difficult methodologies

nodes.text: Someone trained can lead the group through the matrix, from inside the group or as an outside facilitator.
nodes.label: Someone trained can lead the matrix.

source_refs.locator: p. 3, consultants can be a useful adjunct; p. 7

nodes.text: The group is wary of methods that involve emotion and vulnerability.
nodes.label: The group is wary of emotional methods.

nodes.text: The matrix is worded in the group's own vocabulary and begins with a lighter first pass.
nodes.label: The matrix speaks the group's language.

source_refs.locator: p. 4, ranked until a leading issue emerges
p. 8, email for small, low-trust groups
p. 7, the change leader or facilitator

backlog.label: Find a measure of one capacity that two assessors would agree on.
backlog.note: The summary’s assessments are interviews, surveys and existing records, without a stated scoring method.

nodes.text: Members disagree about what the main problem is.
nodes.label: Members disagree about the main problem.

nodes.text: Orient: collect candidate issues, rank them and agree one with clear success criteria.
nodes.label: Orient: agree one issue and what success means.
nodes.proposed_role: Change leader or facilitator, with the whole group

nodes.text: The group has one agreed issue and knows what success looks like.
nodes.label: One agreed issue, with success criteria.

nodes.text: Nobody has a shared picture of the environment or the group's capacities.
nodes.label: No shared picture of environment or capacities.

nodes.text: Assess: interview and survey leaders, members and clients about volatility, hazard, coordination, adaptability and robustness.
nodes.label: Assess: interview and survey about the five factors.
nodes.proposed_role: Facilitator, with leaders, members and clients

nodes.text: There is shared information on the environment and on the group's 24 principles.
nodes.label: Shared data on the environment and 24 principles.

nodes.text: It is unclear which capacity to work on first.
nodes.label: It is unclear which capacity to work on.

nodes.text: Analyse: compare the capacities with the environment and choose the one capacity to adjust.
nodes.label: Analyse: choose the capacity to adjust.

nodes.text: The group has chosen one capacity to improve.
nodes.label: One capacity chosen to improve.

nodes.text: Fear keeps the real obstacles unspoken.
nodes.label: Fear keeps the real obstacles unspoken.

source_refs.locator: p. 7, too unsafe to risk being vulnerable

nodes.text: Adjust: work through the ACT matrix in a format that suits the group.
nodes.label: Adjust: work through the matrix together.
nodes.proposed_role: Change leader or facilitator, with the whole group

nodes.text: The group has agreed how it will act to move toward the improved capacity.
nodes.label: Agreed ways of acting toward the capacity.

nodes.text: Whether the adjustment worked is not yet known.
nodes.label: Nobody knows yet whether it worked.

nodes.text: Repeat: reassess the environment and capacities, and stop once the success criteria are met.
nodes.label: Repeat: reassess, and stop when criteria are met.

nodes.text: Either the criteria are met or the next cycle starts from new information.
nodes.label: Criteria met, or a new cycle starts.

source_refs.locator: p. 8, The group goes back to step 2, Assess

backlog.label: Find a group willing to try one cycle.
backlog.note: No group, facilitator, owner or date is assigned. Existing conditions are illustrative, not observations of a group.
